ideas.title: The island has a ring
ideas.critique: This is round 2's 'I throw too hard' again, and it scores the same: real integrated orbits that precess and spread into a ring all day are physics the island never had, and the ring's striped shadow on the meadow is a strong traced picture. The danger is the plainest version, a scripted Pinchy loop and a texture ring. Collecting launches the game already makes rather than Lumi's throws is better, but only if those launches really are fast enough and really happen.

ideas.title: The island you can only hear
ideas.critique: This is round 2's sonar with the shouting game removed, so it keeps the new look and loses the reason to play: you mostly watch, apart from your own footsteps. Rings for every sound, crossing over the meadow with snores, xylophone colours and sneezes, are a picture of their own. But without hide and seek it slides toward a night-lighting still, a form the island has already used.

ideas.title: Slingshot
ideas.critique: Round 2's black marble with a new payoff: friends using the pull on purpose and swinging out across the island is a new way the creatures move and a behaviour you can watch them learn. It drops the heap that the rope tangle already did. 'Learn' is where it will fail if each swing is scripted, and the lensing ring is still the strongest light idea of the session, as long as it really bends the island into a ring and doesn't blur it.

ideas.title: Cut open
ideas.critique: A clip plane with filled cut faces sweeping the whole island is a new way to see it, and the cottage as a doll's house and the hill's layers would make good traced frames. The insides are the weak part: berries, a word and Pinchy's heart are props placed inside bodies, the see-through Lumi-with-something-inside gag again, and once the sweep has passed there is nothing to watch again.

ideas.title: Noon falls up
ideas.critique: Flipping the island's gravity for a minute is the whole-island upheaval again, the seesaw and the flood. Friends falling, landing and looking up are the beats anyone would guess. A wobbling water blob and clouds you can walk on are the only new parts, and the plainest version is a scripted minute that returns everything to where it was.
